title: CYBRIK resource-bounds error v1
description: Sanitized resource-accounting error. RES_* is deliberately disjoint from budget_exceeded and the BUDGET_* family. Binding: this is the standalone failure document for every res-* operation that has no dedicated result schema. A refused cybrik.res-release.v1, a refused cybrik.res-root-closure.v1, and a refused cybrik.res-reservation-request.v1 are all reported by binding this schema directly; there is no res-release-result, no res-cancel-result, and no per-operation error schema. cybrik.res-reservation-result.v1 embeds this schema by $ref only because admission is all-or-nothing, so the admit/deny outcome and its accounting deltas are one atomic record and the failure travels inside it; that embedding is the exception, not the definition, and is not this schema's only carrier. Conversely this schema is never a ledger record: it carries no root, no sequence, no virtual_time_ms, and no confers_authority, and it is never admissible as a replay event payload in its own right — a failure is reported about the ledger, never entered into it. retriable is derived from code and is advisory only: it grants no capacity, reservation, admission, queue position, priority, authority, capability, permission, delegation, or approval, and relaxes nothing about fail-closed handling. Status: PROPOSED — NOT ACCEPTED — NOT IMPLEMENTED, v0.1.0; not a bundle tag.

retriable.description: Advisory, code-derived hint. It is true exactly when a byte-identical re-issue of the same request could later succeed because peer state changed, and false wherever the caller must change the bytes or the condition is a permanent truth violation. It confers nothing.
